name: Question 20
problem: Consider the function $f(x)={2}^{x}-7.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(9).$
worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(9),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(9)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(9))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(9).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(9)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(9) & =x \\ f(x) & =9 \\ {2}^{x}-7 & =9 \\ {2}^{x} & =16 \\ {2}^{x} & ={2}^{4} \\ x & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(9)=4.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(4),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={2}^{x}-7 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(4) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{4} \\ {f}^{′}(4) & =16\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(9) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(9))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(4)} \\  & =\frac{1}{16\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Consider the function f(x)=2x−7. Given that y=f(x) is invertible throughout its domain, determine (f−1)′(9).

a
116ln⁡(9)
b
14ln⁡(2)
c
116ln⁡(2)
d
19ln⁡(2)
e
14ln⁡(9)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To determine (f−1)′(9), we use the following formula: (f−1)′(9)=1f′(f−1(9))

First, we calculate the value of f−1(9). To do this, we solve the equation f−1(9)=x. This gives f−1(9)=xf(x)=92x−7=92x=162x=24x=4.

Therefore, f−1(9)=4.

Now, we calculate f′(4), as follows: f(x)=2x−7f′(x)=ln⁡2⋅2xf′(4)=ln⁡2⋅24f′(4)=16ln⁡2

Finally, we get (f−1)′(9)=1f′(f−1(9))=1f′(4)=116ln⁡(2).
